Subject: Scoped request: short-term reserved buffer + OEM alignment (RW-2027-1489)

Hi Elena / Carlos —

Following up from last week's partner sync: the Nebula deal (RW-2027-1489) will require a modest on‑ramp of dedicated capacity tied to their Q4 launch. Before we formalize any commitment, we need a practical coordination plan that hedges OEM lead‑time risk and secures a cloud safety lane. High level asks: 

- Elena: can Nebula confirm whether they can accept staged capacity increments (e.g., 40% -> 70% -> 100%) over 12 weeks? Also need their expected steady-state concurrency profile.
- Carlos: please confirm OEM ETA variance for 4k-card SKUs and whether you can provide an "escrow" allocation that is convertible to Redwood reserved capacity.
- Ben / Karthik / Marissa: internal alignment on pricing carveouts and fallback to cloud burst.

To make decisions quickly, please review the attached quote (nebulacloud_quote_v2.pdf) and the vendor leadtime table (vendor_leadtime_table.xlsx). Proposed mitigation options we can discuss:

1) Short-term reserved buffer (30–50 GPUs) bought on a month-to-month basis for 3 months, with conversion credits if OEM fulfillment is delayed.
2) Cloud safety lane: Nebula provides a soft capacity reservation for the launch window with pre-agreed pricing tiers for per-token billing during bursts.
3) Escrow option with OEM: vendor holds a tranche assigned to Redwood and Nebula — Redwood pays a reduced hold fee that converts to reserved capacity on acceptance.

Goal: agree on a path that avoids hard commit until OEM ETAs are firm, but gives the customer predictability for launch. Can we aim for a short call Wednesday (Aug 18) 10am PT to lock the approach?

Thanks,
Mina

Thanks Mina — quick answers from OEM side: 

- ETA variance: for the 4k‑class cards we are seeing quoted fulfillment windows of 8–14 weeks depending on region. Lead-time is still queue-driven; we can provide a sliding ETA that updates weekly.
- Escrow allocation: we can carve out a tranche if Redwood signs a three month "hold" agreement. Hold fee would be 8% of MSRP per month; conversion reduces fee pro‑rata.
- Flexibility: we can offer convertible SKUs (same performance family) that can be swapped prior to deployment if a later batch is delayed.

Action items for us: I'll send a short addendum template that defines "hold" terms and conversion mechanics. Attaching a one‑page ETA matrix in the vendor_leadtime_table.xlsx.

Carlos

Mina / team — thanks for the clear framing. Quick clarifications from Nebula: 

- Staged capacity: Nebula is comfortable with a 3‑phase ramp (35%, 70%, 100%) across 10 weeks if we can guarantee a minimal on-call support SLA during ramp.
- Pricing: Nebula prefers per-node burst pricing rather than a flat conversion credit; they want transparency on what the cloud safety lane will cost during the first 6 weeks.
- Launch window: target September 28–30 for public beta; hard launch later in Q4.

On the call this morning we sketched a hybrid approach: Redwood signs a 3‑month hold with OEM for 40 GPUs (convertible), Nebula provides a soft safety lane of up to 60 concurrent nodes for the launch dates at tiered pricing, and Redwood commits to a post-launch review to decide whether to convert the hold into a reserved contract.

Next steps I propose:
- Ben: scope the short-term pricing comparison (OEM hold vs cloud safety lane) and show token economics for the 3 ramp points.
- Karthik: confirm whether Redwood can accelerate provisioning if OEM provides partial deliverables (e.g., deliver 20 GPUs now, remainder later).
- Mina: please own the conversion terms draft (Carlos will send his addendum) and circulate for legal review.

Happy to join a short follow-up if helpful.

Best,
Elena
Elena Rossi
Head of Platform, Nebula Cloud

All — summary and requested deliverables (so we have a clear runbook ahead of Nebula beta):

Summary:
- OEM can hold 40 convertible GPUs under a 3‑month hold (8% monthly fee) with weekly ETA updates.
- Nebula will provide a cloud safety lane of up to 60 nodes for launch dates with tiered burst pricing.
- Proposed conversion trigger: post‑beta review within 14 days of launch. If OEM fulfillment slips beyond 14 days of expected delivery, Redwood can extend the hold or convert partial hold to a temporary cloud reservation at negotiated rates.

Deliverables (owners):
- Ben: pricing comparison doc (OEM hold vs cloud safety lane) — due Monday Aug 23 (internal spreadsheet + one‑pager).
- Karthik: feasibility note on incremental provisioning and service-level changes if partial OEM shipments land earlier — due Aug 24.
- Mina: draft conversion/hold terms incorporating Carlos' addendum — circulate to Legal by Aug 25.
- Marissa: update customer MLP (mutual action plan) with staged ramp and expectations — share to drive link by Aug 25.

Risks and mitigation:
- Risk: OEM ETA slips beyond launch window. Mitigation: Nebula safety lane + option to increase cloud burst budget for two weeks.
- Risk: Price delta too high for customer. Mitigation: include conversion credits and clear refund/credit schedule in hold agreement.

I'll assemble the pricing comparison template and ping the group when it's ready. If anyone needs to reassign tasks, reply with the updated owner.

Thanks — Ben
